function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a natural phenomenon has been known since ancient times (e.g., static electricity observed by Thales of Miletus). However, systematic study and understanding began with figures such as William Gilbert (who coined the term “electricity”), Benjamin Franklin (the lightning‑rod experiments), Alessandro Volta (invented the voltaic pile), and later scientists who developed the laws of electromagnetism. Thus, there isn’t a single discoverer—many contributed to uncovering and harnessing electrical phenomena.
